result.summary: Candidate 03-mutations-01:1 is confirmed, with a narrower mechanism than the candidate states. Once an attempt enters `reconciliation-required`, neither client has a transition out of it. This is safe when a mutation may still be unknown. It is not safe in the expired-on-receipt branch, where nothing was sent, so the outcome is known. The candidate's claim that the daemon answers `not-seen` for an expired ticket is wrong. The daemon answers `reconciliation-required`, but that gives the same stuck result. No other defects were found in the supplied files.

findings.trigger: A ticket arrives with `expiresAt` already past (client/daemon clock skew or a slow ticket reply). The controller sets `reconciliation-required` and releases the request without ever calling `mutate`. The user then presses Reconcile, or tries to edit or delete the same connection.
findings.defect: The record is stuck. `reconciliation-required` is in `blocking`, so `isBlocked(key)` rejects every later `submit`/`remove` for that key with `busy`. `canDismiss` is false for this phase, and `canReplay` is false because the request was released. Reconcile calls daemon `status`. For an expired ticket with no receipt, the daemon returns `reconciliation-required` (management.ts:416), so `#status` sets the same phase again (controller.ts:162). The only exit is a workbench reload or `dispose()`. In this branch no mutation was sent, so the outcome is known not to have committed. Keeping the key blocked therefore protects no unknown state.
findings.evidence: controller.ts:43 (`blocking` includes the phase). controller.ts:62 (`canDismiss` excludes it). controller.ts:67 (`isBlocked`). controller.ts:90 (the expired-on-receipt branch sets the phase and calls `#release`, before the `#mutate` call at line 94). controller.ts:162 and 176 (every later transition returns to the same phase). management.ts:416-417 (an expired ticket with no receipt returns `reconciliation-required`; `not-seen` is returned only at line 420, after that check). management-tickets.ts:158 (expired tickets are never silently `not-seen`). Kotlin ConnectionMutationController.kt:144-147, 259 and 277 have the same path. The LLD §3.6 requires 'expired/unreceipted => reconciliation-required, no replay' and a reconciliation record before a new target mutation. It does not say the record can never be resolved in-session.
findings.remedy: Keep the no-replay rule and the LLD phase name. Add an explicit resolution for the case where nothing was sent. In the expired-on-receipt branch (TS line 90, Kotlin 144), end the attempt as a dismissible `ticket-error`-class phase with a fixed 'ticket expired before submit, nothing was sent' code. Do not use `reconciliation-required` there. For an expired ticket after a mutation was sent, add an explicit acknowledge or dismiss step. It would be offered only after daemon `status` reports no receipt and the authoritative list refresh succeeds. It would release the block without any replay. Apply the change in the TS and Kotlin controllers. Add a parity test for: expired ticket, Reconcile, then a new submit on the same key. If product policy needs the block to stay for the post-send case, resolve that separately.

obligations.evidence: Confirmed with a correction. `blocking` (controller.ts:43) includes `reconciliation-required`. `canDismiss` (line 62) excludes it. `canReplay` needs a retained request and an unexpired ticket. Line 90 releases the request without sending. Reconcile on an expired, unreceipted ticket gets `reconciliation-required` from the daemon (management.ts:416). The candidate says the daemon returns `not-seen`; it does not (the `not-seen` return at line 420 comes after that check). Line 162 still maps the result back to the same phase. The Kotlin controller has the same path. The LLD allows a reload to reset state, but it does not require an in-session dead end. The no-send branch is clearly safe to resolve.

limitations: The UI and view layers were not supplied. I could not check whether they offer an exit other than the controller's `dismiss`, `replay` or `reconcile`.
`decodeOperationStatus` in wire.ts was not supplied. I assumed it passes the daemon's `reconciliation-required` status through to line 162.
The temporary-scope daemon path was not supplied. I checked only the saved-scope ticket inspection and status code.
I did not assess other candidates, the UI acceptance status or the pending external service coverage.
evidenceRequests: The view-layer code that renders `reconciliation-required` records and their available actions.
Controller tests covering ticket-expired followed by Reconcile followed by a new submit.
